question: In a country that exported large quantities of food while keeping most industry in private hands, how did daily working hours compare between large factories and smaller craft workshops?
Given what share of the industrial workforce women made up, what proportion of a male worker's earnings could a woman in the same factory expect to receive?

What was the specific internal division within a group that one political leader used to argue it could not serve as the unified driving force of a revolution, even though a rival faction believed it could?
How many people were already refusing to work in the capital when the march that ended in bloodshed took place, and what workplace incident had set the whole sequence of events in motion?
What two separate breakdowns — one cutting the country off from outside goods, one collapsing from within — combined to force small production units to shut down entirely?
On what exact date did the monarch step down, and what was peculiar about the location where the body that had come to replace his authority first assembled?

After losing a popular vote, what did the leader of the ruling faction claim was a more genuinely democratic institution, and what reasoning did he give for shutting down the one the people had just elected?
Despite receiving military support from four foreign governments, why did the forces opposing the revolution end up losing the backing of the very population they needed to govern?
During the years when the state set all prices centrally, by how much did combined output in the three heaviest industries grow, and across which specific years did this growth occur?

What did those in power believe rural producers were doing with their grain rather than selling it, and how did this suspicion lead directly to a complete transformation in how agricultural land was owned?

By the time a country's own citizens acknowledged that their system of rule had drifted from its founding ideals, what body had that same country already created to export those ideals to workers elsewhere in the world?
After funding another country's war of independence, what was the total debt burden the French state was carrying, and how much were creditors charging annually to keep lending?
Over roughly how long a period did the French population increase by around five million, and what recurring crisis did this growth help produce whenever the harvest failed?

What kinds of commercial activity had given rise to the social group that most strongly championed the idea that a person's standing should reflect their effort rather than their parentage, and what form of government did Rousseau argue this implied?
Although one group at the 1789 assembly was twice as large as each of the other two, why did its size give it no advantage when it came to the actual outcome of votes?
When a major institution lost both its right to collect income from the population and its ownership of land in a single legislative session, how much did the state stand to gain from the seizure?
What expansion of voting rights was introduced immediately after crowds seized the royal household, and what age threshold did the new rules set?

When the most radical phase of the political upheaval came to an end with the execution of its leader, what happened to ordinary citizens' ability to participate in choosing their government under the system that replaced it?

How many organisations did women manage to build across the country to push for their rights, and what did the revolutionary government — which those same women had helped bring to power — ultimately do to all of them?
Which two home ports did traders use as their starting point in a three-way commercial network, and who supplied them with the human beings they carried onward to the plantations?

What approval process had to be completed before any written or staged work could reach an audience under the old system, and what visibly happened across the country the moment that requirement was removed?
What were the two concrete administrative changes the self-crowned ruler introduced that continued to shape everyday life in other countries long after his military defeat?
